Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No public PI‑SPI rulebook/scheme rules located on BCEAO public pages; while BCEAO provides general payment systems description, no downloadable PI‑SPI rulebook was found via searches for "PI‑SPI rulebook", "règles du schéma PI‑SPI" and BCEAO PI‑SPI documentation.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (0/Unknown, no source) understated public availability of scheme rules. BCEAO operates a public PI-SPI documentation centre (pispi.bceao.int/chiffres-cles) offering downloadable regulatory texts, technical reports and tutorials, and publishes the governing legal instrument, Instruction N°001-01-2024 relative aux services de paiement dans l'UMOA (dated January 2024), as a PDF on its site; a separate developer portal (developer.pispi.bceao.int/guides) publishes API integration guides. Score revised from 0 to 3 (Yes - Fully Public).
revised_comments: The Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO) publishes the rules governing the PI-SPI instant payment system, which covers Burkina Faso as a WAEMU/UMOA member state, at a dedicated public documentation centre (pispi.bceao.int) offering downloadable regulatory texts, technical reports and tutorials without registration. The core legal instrument, Instruction N°001-01-2024 relative aux services de paiement dans l'UMOA, is published in full on the BCEAO website, and a separate developer portal provides publicly accessible API integration guides for participants.

Definition: Whether digital payment systems and access points (apps, USSD, agents) are designed to accommodate persons with disabilities (visual, hearing, mobility, cognitive impairments), and disability-disaggregated coverage rates if data available.
Comments: No credible Burkina Faso-specific evidence found for disability accessibility requirements in digital payments (e.g., accessibility standards for apps/USSD, disability-inclusive financial inclusion policy). Searched for disability accessibility and payments in Burkina Faso without finding authoritative policy/program evidence.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (0/Unknown, no source) is superseded by G3ict's Digital Accessibility Rights Evaluation (DARE) Index country profile for Burkina Faso, an authoritative cross-country accessibility benchmark, which records 0/50 on 'Country Policies and Programs Outcomes by Areas of ICT Accessibility', with explicit 'No policy' ratings for mobile telephony, e-government/smart cities for all, assistive technologies for independent living, and accessible procurement, and no process for involving disabled persons' organisations in ICT accessibility policymaking. No Burkina Faso-specific evidence of accessible design in mobile money apps, USSD menus or agent networks was found in supporting searches. Score revised from 0 to 1 (No). G3ict data covers general ICT accessibility policy (most recent update circa 2020) rather than payments specifically, so treat with medium confidence.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso has no documented policy requiring accessibility accommodations for persons with disabilities across mobile telephony, e-government services or assistive technologies, and there is no process for involving disabled persons' organisations in ICT accessibility policymaking, per the G3ict Digital Accessibility Rights Evaluation Index. No specific accessibility features (screen-reader support, voice interfaces, accessible agent services) are documented for digital payment channels such as mobile money apps or USSD menus.
